title: St. Joe-Benton Harbor News
text:
David Vollrath, 1st District Commissioner | Berrien County
David Vollrath, 1st District Commissioner | Berrien County
The Berrien County Health Department (BCHD) is highlighting its HIV prevention, testing, and education services in recognition of World AIDS Day on December 1. The department aims to increase awareness about the importance of HIV testing and ongoing prevention efforts.
World AIDS Day, observed each year on December 1, brings people together globally to support those living with HIV and promote continued attention to prevention and treatment. The day also marks the start of HIV/AIDS Awareness Month, a national initiative that focuses on the impact of HIV/AIDS locally and worldwide.
BCHD offers confidential HIV services through state-certified nurses and community health workers who provide testing in a safe environment. During visits, staff discuss risk factors with clients, offer prevention education, and help individuals create plans to reduce their risk of infection.
“Our goal is to normalize testing and connect people to the care they need,” said Emma Yazel, STD/HIV community health worker at BCHD. “By offering accessible services in a welcoming environment, we’re helping residents protect their health and the health of the community.”
Rapid HIV tests are available at BCHD offices, delivering results in about 20 minutes. Staff review confidential results on the same day and connect anyone who tests positive for HIV with medical care and support services.
The department also provides referrals for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which can be taken as a daily pill or periodic injection to help prevent HIV transmission for those who test negative.
Appointments for these services are offered Monday through Thursday at both BCHD’s Benton Harbor office at 2149 E. Napier Ave., from 1-4 p.m., and its Niles office at 1205 N. Front St., from 9-11 a.m. and 1-4 p.m. Community members can schedule appointments online or by calling 269.926.7121.
According to recommendations from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), everyone between ages 13-64 should get tested for HIV at least once as part of routine healthcare. Those with certain risk factors—including men who have sex with men, individuals with multiple sexual partners since their last test, people who have shared needles or injection equipment, or those diagnosed with other sexually transmitted infections—are encouraged to get tested annually.
More information about BCHD’s HIV services is available at berriencounty.org/637/HIV-Services.
